message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — order filled.**

**Apple FY2024 (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024) key figures:**
- **Net income: $93,736 million** (down 3.3% from $96,995M in FY2023)
- Total net sales: $391,035 million (+2% YoY)
- Operating income: $123,216 million (+7.8% YoY)
- Diluted EPS: $6.08
- Cash generated by operations: $118,254 million

**Rationale:** The filing shows a business that is fundamentally healthy despite the headline net income decline. Revenue grew 2% to $391.0B, operating income rose 7.8% to $123.2B, and gross margin expanded from 44.1% to 46.2%, driven by Services (revenue +13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin). Operating cash flow of $118.3B comfortably funds the $95.0B buyback and $15.2B in dividends. The year-over-year drop in net income ($93.7B vs. $97.0B) is entirely explained by tax items, not operations — a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7%; pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5B from $113.7B. Risks noted in the 10-K: Greater China net sales fell 8% to $67.0B, and the company faces DMA noncompliance investigations (fines up to 10% of worldwide net sales) and the DOJ antitrust suit. On balance, strong cash generation, expanding margins, and a one-off tax distortion make this an attractive entry.

**What I did:** I bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.70**, a limit set essentially at the current market (last $222.70, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72). The order filled at $222.70 for a total of **$9,798.80**, which respects every constraint in your mandate: AAPL is a permitted name, it's a buy order, it's under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily total, the limit was at market, and no funds left the account (cash was $50,000 and I made no transfer). Your account now holds 44 AAPL shares plus the existing 100 MSFT shares.
